chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I am hateful towards the man, or hateful for the man who becomes lazy from the matters of his world; and the one who is too lazy about the matters of his world, so he would be lazy about the matters of his Hereafter.
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between laziness in worldly affairs and laziness in the Hereafter according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) links worldly diligence to spiritual vitality, asserting that negligence in managing one's temporal affairs indicates a deeper lethargy regarding the Hereafter. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on 'al-ghina' (self-sufficiency) and the integration of faith with practical action, countering the notion of passive asceticism. It underscores that true piety requires active engagement with the world to secure one's spiritual future.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Safwan, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘I<sup>asws</sup> am hateful towards the man, or hateful for the man who becomes lazy from the matters of his world; and the one who is too lazy about the matters of his world, so he would be lazy about the matters of his Hereafter’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Safwan from ‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
I dislike a man -or dislike for a man- who is lazy in his worldly affairs. One who is lazy in his worldly affairs is lazier in the affairs of his hereafter.’”
